extracted.intended_audience: NLP researchers and practitioners working on clickbait detection and related news/headline modelling
extracted.subtask_description: Developing and evaluating models that detect (and mitigate/spoil) clickbait headlines using a combination of embeddings and linguistically motivated informativeness features; includes benchmarking against standard baselines and releasing code/models for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model performance (F1-score)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall detection quality is measured using F1-score; the paper reports a best-performing model achieving an F1-score of 91%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use F1 (harmonic mean of precision and recall) as a primary performance metric when comparing clickbait detectors; report numeric scores and compare to baselines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid modelling approach (embeddings + informativeness features)
rubrics_metrics.description: Combine transformer-based text embeddings with linguistically motivated informativeness features (the authors' best model is 'XGBoost over embeddings augmented with 15 explicit features').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Augment dense embeddings with explicit, interpretable features rather than relying solely on embeddings or feature-only models; tree-based learners (e.g., XGBoost) can be used on the combined representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit informativeness / linguistic features
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature set that enhances interpretability by highlighting salient linguistic cues such as second-person pronouns, superlatives, numerals, and attention-oriented punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineer and include explicit linguistic/informativeness features (examples given: second-person pronouns, superlatives, numerals, attention-oriented punctuation) because they improve transparency and help identify why a headline is classified as clickbait.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative evaluation against multiple baselines
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate improvement relative to TF-IDF, Word2Vec, GloVe, LLM prompt-based classification, and feature-only baselines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Benchmark new detectors against a variety of baselines spanning classical vectorizers, word-embedding models, LLM-prompt approaches, and feature-only systems to establish empirical gains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and evaluation of vectorizers/embeddings and classifiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate classical vectorizers, word embedding baselines, and large language model embeddings paired with tree-based classifiers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systematically compare different text representations (TF-IDF, Word2Vec, GloVe, transformer/LLM embeddings) and classifier families (including tree-based models) to identify best-performing combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability and calibration of predictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed feature set enhances interpretability and enables transparent and well-calibrated clickbait predictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor designs that provide human-interpretable signals for decisions (e.g., feature attribution) and assess calibration (confidence reliability) of classifiers in addition to accuracy metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility (release of code and trained models)
rubrics_metrics.description: Release code and trained models to support reproducible research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide code, trained model artifacts, and data/implementation details so others can reproduce results and build on the work.
